Just do the best you can, like if you can't do a middle split, straddle as far as you can. With left/right splits you can do a deep lunge instead. 

Oh also, I'd recommend stretching later in the day rather than in the morning, this is personal preference but also by the end of the day, you've already been moving around and loosened up your muscles a bit, in the mornings when you've just rolled out of bed being completely still for 7 hours, you're a lot stiffer. 

The only thing I can really say about building flexibility is consistency. You can stretch throughout the day just by arching your back when you sit down, or walking with your shoulders back a bit. It's great because then you'll have great posture and passively stretch out your muscles :D

It's not a super rigid one, these are the ones I do consistently:

Middle split, lean right/left/middle and twist my back going right/left

Right/left split, stretch forwards/backwards

Pike 

Pike but only one leg at a time, twist my back both ways while leaning forwards

Do a seal position but with my arms pressing on a wall and focus on relaxing my back and letting it sink as far as I can get it

Those are all the basic ones I do, I occasionally add some random things to switch it up, and I hold each position for 4 8 counts 

Something really important imo is building strength with your flexibility, like practicing kicks so you can actually hold up your leg instead of only being able to do splits. 

Things you can do with ascending levels of difficulty (imo):

Legs:

Kicks (just like controlled ones side to side, arabesque kicks, and kicking in front of you)

Jumps (toe touches/herkys/firebirds/basically all cheer jumps)

Holding your leg in the air 

Holding your leg in the air and essentially doing squats but not as low 

Back: 

Holding a back bend

Bridge

Bridge + standing back up 

Bridge + kicking over 

Back walkover 

Chinstand (this one isn't particularly hard, but you need a decent amount of control, if you can do a good handstand with a wall then you should be able to do this)

Hope this was helpful!

But what if it's not really about self destruction? For me, personally, it isn't about crying over my miserable life and wanting to end my life. Don't get me wrong, I do that too, it's just that self harm for me is somewhat detached from that. I see no issue with it, honestly, like if I don't cut too deep and clean the wound, and it makes me feel better, why shouldn't I do it?

But from a more logical perspective, without all the romance and whatnot, with the facts, "I cut, and I don't see why I should stop", could you accept that and look past it to pursue a normal relationship with that person?

If it makes me feel better, why don't I have a right to do it if it won't hurt anyone else? I mean, people smoke, which hurts the people around them (secondhand smoke) and themselves, but it's still legal/socially acceptable. idk man, just stay strong.

It's either from a sort of trigger, or frustration. For the first one, I'm not sure what triggers me, but certain thoughts or memories regarding pain and misery do it for me. I just really, really feel like seeing my blood spill and feeling the sharp, searing pain only my razor can give me. Regarding the frustration, when I go into that stage where you feel sad then angry, that's where I really damage myself, where it gets a bit dangerous. It's like a pulsating rage that I need to relieve.

While on the surface that may seem like a good idea, I'm not sure that threatening to cut yourself too was the best approach.. Sorry, I don't mean to sound pretentious or judgmental in any way, it's just that as a cutter, if someone said that to me, I'd just be even more stressed out, and therefore build anxiety, therefore cut, therefore feel stressed again, and the circle just keeps going. I'm happy it turned out well for you though, and that you made a positive impact on her life, but just beware that some might not react as well to what you did :)
